# 3. Data and Empirical Strategy

Our sample is an unbalanced panel of 2,840 S&P 1500 firms from 2004 to 2019. We regress Tobin's q on the fraction of independent directors, controlling for size, leverage, and industry and year fixed effects, and cluster standard errors by firm. Because board composition is chosen by the firm, these estimates describe associations; we do not claim to identify the effect of independence.

# 4. Results

Table 3 reports the estimates. Board independence is associated with higher firm value: a ten-percentage-point higher independent share goes with a Tobin's q 0.06 higher (t = 3.1). The association is twice as large in firms with dispersed ownership, consistent with independent directors monitoring where shareholders cannot, though it could also reflect firms with better prospects choosing more independent boards. Independence is also correlated with lower CEO pay in the same firms (Table 4).
